capabilities: Render the vault graph as an animated 3D brain via WebGL2
Map notes to anatomical regions from frontmatter, tags, folders, and link behavior
Open a note by clicking its node and pin nodes by dragging
Toggle regions and labels, and dim or restore lobes
Apply performance presets and a light Daylight palette
disambiguation: Not an anatomical or medical reference tool; it draws your own vault graph in the shape of a brain.
extras: Mobile support is explicitly experimental and depends on device performance; a Canvas2D fallback runs when WebGL2 is unavailable; rendering is local-only with no network requests; the manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
problem: Obsidian's built-in graph view shows the vault as a flat 2D node layout, with no way to place notes meaningfully in distinct spatial regions.

relations.evidence: You might also like Cerebro Mycelium, which renders your vault as a 2D living fungal network.

summary: Vault graph visualization that renders notes and links as an animated 3D anatomical brain, with notes grouped into brain regions by type.
